about: Tax and percentage discounts. Half up, away from zero, once per line.

cases.name: a rate of zero takes nothing
a rate of one takes everything
zero taxed at any rate is zero
exactly half rounds up, not to even
cases.about: 200 at 2.5% is 5.00 exactly; 50 at 5% is 2.5, the half case. Banker's rounding would give 2 here and a customer comparing two identical receipts would see different totals.

cases.name: a negative amount rounds away from zero, not toward it
cases.about: A refund line is the mirror of the sale line that created it. Rounding a refund toward zero would return a cent less than was taken, every time, in the shop's favour.

cases.name: a negative rate on a positive amount
a negative rate on a negative amount is positive
a rate with no decimal point
trailing zeros in the rate do not change the answer
six decimal places, the deepest a cost is allowed
a safe result may require a wider intermediate
cases.about: Half of the largest bigint fits in bigint, but multiplying that amount by the scaled rate overflows a 64-bit intermediate before division.

cases.name: a rate that is not a number is refused
a rate in exponent notation is refused
cases.about: Accepting it would mean parsing a float somewhere, which is the one thing this type exists to prevent.
